normalizations.reason: After returning to the normal screen the absolute cursor row reflects each product's transcript height. Process exit compares exitCode, active screen, cursor visibility and private modes instead. No editor state is normalised.
Pi renders a path label without the leading @ while its value carries the marker. One leading @ is removed from the display label only; candidate identity and order are still compared exactly.
The "(n/m)" position row reports the visible slice of the candidate list. It is recorded separately and excluded from candidate identities.

Temporary directory names and file modes are product internals. Both products create a 0700 directory; Pi writes the prompt with mode 0644 and PiSharp with 0600. The captured prompt text, editor result, provider text and terminal restoration are compared exactly.

knownDifferences.summary: Pi completes with fuzzyFilter over its builtin command list; PiSharp uses the shared ordered catalogue with prefix matching and registers additional implemented commands. Pi also appends a trailing space and closes the picker when an explicit Tab resolves a single candidate, and exposes argument completion for /model. PiSharp applies without the trailing space and has no argument completion.
knownDifferences.closure: Port fuzzyFilter, align the completion-visible command catalogue and implement argument completion; none of these is a bounded editor correction.

knownDifferences.summary: Pi auto-triggers @ completion through an fd fuzzy walk, scores and orders entries, and applies a file with a trailing space after the closing quote. PiSharp only computes path candidates on Tab using readdir prefix matching, so the automatic overlay is absent and application places the cursor before the closing quote.
knownDifferences.closure: Implement the fd-based fuzzy path provider and its application/cursor rules.
